before.supportingExcerpt: Fictional splice-site example: 32 alternate reads among 160 usable reads give VAF 20 per cent. Suppose half the sampled cells are malignant, every cell has two local copies, and each affected cancer cell carries one altered copy, with equal recovery per copy. Then VAF = purity times cancer-cell fraction divided by two; 0.20 = 0.50 times CCF divided by two gives CCF 80 per cent. With pure cancer-cell input, the same 20 per cent fits CCF 40 per cent. These are model calculations, not counted cells. Local copy changes, altered-copy multiplicity, recovery bias or uncertain purity can change the fit. A measured splice junction and functional repair remain separate questions.

before.supportingExcerpt: Biallelic inactivation concerns whether either parental contribution still supplies useful function in the relevant cancer-cell population, rather than simply counting two physical DNA copies or two events somewhere in a tissue. A damaging change plus loss of the other contribution can support it, but phasing, allele-specific copy state, consequence and cell mixture matter. High VAF alone cannot establish this state. Nguyen and colleagues' pan-cancer analysis associated particular biallelic repair-gene alterations with genomic damage patterns; that association does not make every variant in every repair gene functionally equivalent or establish present drug sensitivity.
before.explanation: Biallelic useful-function loss is in the relevant cells, with phase, copy state and mixture; the pan-cancer association does not equate all variants. complete raw Europe PMC abstract read complete raw Europe PMC abstract read

before.supportingExcerpt: Fictional example. A well has half the metabolic signal but the same identified viable tumour-cell endpoint count as control. This establishes a changed proxy, not half the cells killed; endpoint equality also does not reconstruct every division and death. Separate death, target engagement, safe human dosing and clinical benefit remain questions. This is an arithmetic and interpretation exercise, not observed patient data. Possible readouts include cell number, metabolism, mass, growth and death. Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is a cellular energy molecule measured by some luminescence assays. Promega's primary assay guidance states that cellular ATP content varies with cell type and physiology and can alter the relation between cell number and light output. A lower ATP signal can therefore reflect fewer cells or a per-cell change, rather than a counted death fraction. Source: https://www.promega.com/-/media/files/resources/protocols/technical-bulletins/0/celltiter-glo-luminescent-cell-viability-assay-protocol.pdf

before.supportingExcerpt: Fictional splice-site example: 32 alternate reads among 160 usable reads give VAF 20 per cent. Suppose half the sampled cells are malignant, every cell has two local copies, and each affected cancer cell carries one altered copy, with equal recovery per copy. Then VAF = purity times cancer-cell fraction divided by two; 0.20 = 0.50 times CCF divided by two gives CCF 80 per cent. With pure cancer-cell input, the same 20 per cent fits CCF 40 per cent. These are model calculations, not counted cells. Local copy changes, altered-copy multiplicity, recovery bias or uncertain purity can change the fit. A measured splice junction and functional repair remain separate questions.

before.supportingExcerpt: Biallelic inactivation concerns whether either parental contribution still supplies useful function in the relevant cancer-cell population, rather than simply counting two physical DNA copies or two events somewhere in a tissue. A damaging change plus loss of the other contribution can support it, but phasing, allele-specific copy state, consequence and cell mixture matter. High VAF alone cannot establish this state. Nguyen and colleagues' pan-cancer analysis associated particular biallelic repair-gene alterations with genomic damage patterns; that association does not make every variant in every repair gene functionally equivalent or establish present drug sensitivity.
before.explanation: Biallelic useful-function loss is in the relevant cells, with phase, copy state and mixture; the pan-cancer association does not equate all variants. complete raw Europe PMC abstract read complete raw Europe PMC abstract read

before.supportingExcerpt: Randomised outcome evidence must be assessed for the named assay and use rather than declared absent for all functional testing in solid tumours. Ranjan and colleagues reported a 2023 trial of ChemoID selection versus physician choice from the same chemotherapy list in 78 people with recurrent glioblastoma under the 2016 WHO definition. Enrolment stopped after a prespecified efficacy analysis; the intention-to-treat report gave median overall survival of twelve versus 7.5 months. Participants could provide viable tumour through surgery or biopsy, so the findings do not include every patient with recurrent glioblastoma. Cordgenics supported the assay resources, and two authors declared licensed intellectual-property interests. This is evidence for the studied strategy and population, without validating another assay, organoid system, postoperative breast decision or universal treatment rule.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Assay card for spatial transcriptomics (a reading guide, not a score). Measures and how: RNA with coordinates, by preparing a section, capturing or probing RNA, sequencing or imaging, decoding, registering positions and reporting the assignment rules. Input and tissue cost: protocol-compatible frozen or fixed sections; sectioning and molecular preparation consume allocated material, some workflows alter or destroy the assayed section, and re-scoring existing data consumes no new tissue. Output and units: gene counts per spot, bin or assigned cell, and decoded molecule coordinates, often in micrometres, with physical dimensions, normalisation and observed-versus-imputed labels kept. Thresholds: assay-specific gene or probe coverage, capture and decoding quality, background and segmentation criteria; no universal high-expression or neighbourhood cutoff. Failure modes: poor RNA, incomplete probe coverage, low capture, image-registration errors, inaccurate segmentation, spillover and unsuitable reference models. Limits: no automatic single-cell identity, complete transcriptome, whole-tumour representation, proven interaction or clinical selection rule. Validation tier: many workflows are research methods, so check analytical and intended-use validation for the exact assay and model; resolution claims and regulatory status are separate questions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) is the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) system, with two main classes of peptide-display molecule. Classical class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) has a heavy chain, beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a bound peptide, is found on most nucleated cells, usually displays peptides from proteins made inside the cell and is read by CD8 T cells. Class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) has alpha and beta chains with a bound peptide, is mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells (expression can be induced elsewhere), usually displays proteins processed in vesicles, often acquired from outside, and is read by CD4 T cells. These are common routes, not exclusive lists: cross-presentation puts externally acquired antigen on class I without making it class II, and a CD4 response is not proof of matching class I tumour display. CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors and usual recognition partners, not guarantees of cell function. Structural work shows the T-cell receptor lying across the peptide and HLA together (Garboczi et al., 1996), CD8 contacting the class I alpha2 and alpha3 domains and B2M (Gao et al., 1997) and CD4 engaging a separate class II region (Yin et al., 2012); these constructs do not define universal angles or functions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A conventional alpha-beta T-cell receptor uses paired chains to recognise a peptide-HLA surface. Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. CDR3 is an informative variable region, but neither a beta-chain sequence nor CDR3 alone specifies the complete paired receptor or its function.

Particular receptors can cross-react across peptide and HLA contexts; that does not establish a universal cross-reactivity rate. Paired receptor identity, binding, activation, target-cell death and clinical benefit require different evidence. A response by one reconstructed pair to peptide-loaded cells does not establish that another alpha-chain pairing recognises the same target, or that either kills naturally presenting tumour cells. Use irrelevant-target, HLA and target-only viability controls. Peptide loading can bypass natural processing, and contact diagrams are not healthy-tissue safety tests.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Residual tumour here means cancer remaining in the sampled tissue after treatment. For residual-tumour research, first support malignant-cell identity, then ask which recovered states, target messages and immune profiles are present. A stress programme does not establish a genetic clone or explain survival. In Kim and colleagues' twenty-person triple-negative breast-cancer study, longitudinal exome data and single-cell DNA/RNA data in eight participants supported selection of pre-existing genotypes alongside expression reprogramming under the studied treatment. This is not a universal resistance mechanism. Compare the sampled region, time, preparation, recovery and analysis before attributing a difference to treatment; a missing cluster need not have been eliminated. In a separate fictional calculation, an input suspension truly containing 4 percent malignant nuclei gives an expectation of 240 among 6,000 retained profiles only if malignant and other nuclei have equal inclusion through recovery, capture and quality filtering. evidence.supportingExcerpt: DNA contains nucleotide chains with a sugar–phosphate backbone and the bases A, T, C and G. Complementary A–T and C–G pairing joins antiparallel strands. Nuclear chromosomes contain DNA associated with proteins as chromatin; nucleosomes organize DNA around histones. Mitochondria carry a separate genome. A gene is a functional region within DNA, rather than an entire chromosome. Replication copies DNA, while transcription produces RNA from a selected template. Packaging and gene presence do not establish active transcription or a functional protein.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: RNA, short for ribonucleic acid, uses ribose and usually uracil in place of DNA’s thymine. It is often single-stranded but can fold through internal pairing. Messenger RNA carries a coding template; ribosomal RNA contributes to ribosome structure and catalysis; transfer RNA brings amino acids; regulatory RNAs influence other molecules. Many nuclear messages receive a 5-prime cap and poly(A) tail and have introns removed by splicing before translation, but these features are not universal to all RNAs. Ribosomes read a coding sequence in codons to produce a polypeptide; processing, folding and localization follow.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) is the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) system, with two main classes of peptide-display molecule. Classical class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) has a heavy chain, beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a bound peptide, is found on most nucleated cells, usually displays peptides from proteins made inside the cell and is read by CD8 T cells. Class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) has alpha and beta chains with a bound peptide, is mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells (expression can be induced elsewhere), usually displays proteins processed in vesicles, often acquired from outside, and is read by CD4 T cells. These are common routes, not exclusive lists: cross-presentation puts externally acquired antigen on class I without making it class II, and a CD4 response is not proof of matching class I tumour display. CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors and usual recognition partners, not guarantees of cell function. Structural work shows the T-cell receptor lying across the peptide and HLA together (Garboczi et al., 1996), CD8 contacting the class I alpha2 and alpha3 domains and B2M (Gao et al., 1997) and CD4 engaging a separate class II region (Yin et al., 2012); these constructs do not define universal angles or functions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A conventional alpha-beta T-cell receptor uses paired chains to recognise a peptide-HLA surface. Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. CDR3 is an informative variable region, but neither a beta-chain sequence nor CDR3 alone specifies the complete paired receptor or its function.

Particular receptors can cross-react across peptide and HLA contexts; that does not establish a universal cross-reactivity rate. Paired receptor identity, binding, activation, target-cell death and clinical benefit require different evidence. A response by one reconstructed pair to peptide-loaded cells does not establish that another alpha-chain pairing recognises the same target, or that either kills naturally presenting tumour cells. Use irrelevant-target, HLA and target-only viability controls. Peptide loading can bypass natural processing, and contact diagrams are not healthy-tissue safety tests.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Residual tumour here means cancer remaining in the sampled tissue after treatment. For residual-tumour research, first support malignant-cell identity, then ask which recovered states, target messages and immune profiles are present. A stress programme does not establish a genetic clone or explain survival. In Kim and colleagues' twenty-person triple-negative breast-cancer study, longitudinal exome data and single-cell DNA/RNA data in eight participants supported selection of pre-existing genotypes alongside expression reprogramming under the studied treatment. This is not a universal resistance mechanism. Compare the sampled region, time, preparation, recovery and analysis before attributing a difference to treatment; a missing cluster need not have been eliminated. In a separate fictional calculation, an input suspension truly containing 4 percent malignant nuclei gives an expectation of 240 among 6,000 retained profiles only if malignant and other nuclei have equal inclusion through recovery, capture and quality filtering. Tissue-area cellularity is a different denominator. The calculation is neither a yield forecast nor an adequacy cutoff.
